topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, contextual background, and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer evolution.

topics.label: Clonal selection and epigenetic drivers in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how successive genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations confer competitive growth advantages through Darwinian clonal evolution.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell hierarchy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the hierarchical models of tumor initiation to examine whether stemness properties and specific cell types of origin are required for malignancy.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory promotion of tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate that genetic alterations require non-mutational promotional signals and supportive stromal microenvironments to drive malignant transformation and growth.

topics.label: Research methods and synthesis of cancer evolutionary mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the modern spatial and single-cell profiling techniques used to investigate tumor biology and summarize the lecture's integrated evolutionary framework.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing and previews the topic of the upcoming lecture.
